answer: On directed graph datasets, LINE is generally reported to outperform DeepWalk on downstream node classification. In the original LINE paper, LINE achieved higher Micro-F1 than DeepWalk on the directed citation network Cora, with the reported Micro-F1 being about 0.83 for LINE versus about 0.81 for DeepWalk (exact values can vary slightly by split and implementation). The main reason is that LINE explicitly models first- and second-order proximity and can better preserve asymmetric relationships in directed graphs, whereas DeepWalk’s random-walk objective is less tailored to directionality.
